comparison: Both strongly support ETBR expression in SGCs and ET-1 expression in endothelial cells (C2, C3, C28, C42-C45, C47-C48). OpenEval emphasizes multi-platform validation across species; peer reviewers accept findings as robust without challenge, with Reviewer 3 calling the study 'well-executed.'

Both support ex vivo evidence that ETBR antagonism enhances axon growth (C4, C49-C54). OpenEval highlights specificity controls; peer reviewers find evidence 'convincing' that ETBR functions as a 'default brake on axon regrowth.' Reviewer 2 requests better representative images but does not challenge conclusions. Both also address C77-C78 regarding aged mice.

Both support in vivo Bosentan efficacy across injury models (C5, C57-C60, C63, C70, C72-C73). OpenEval notes ETAR antagonist controls strengthen ETBR specificity; peer reviewers affirm findings with Reviewer 3 confirming 'primary involvement of the ET-1/ETBR pathway.' Reviewer 2 requests discussion of regeneration kinetics but accepts data.

Both address NGF-induced vs spontaneous growth (C67-C69). OpenEval includes these in broader in vivo support; peer reviewers accept findings but Reviewer 2 requests additional rationale explaining differences between growth conditions and comparison of in vitro/in vivo models.

Both address IENFD trends (C64-C65). OpenEval describes this as 'appropriately preliminary'; peer reviewers note the speculative nature ('may accelerate') and do not specifically comment, suggesting it is viewed as supportive rather than conclusive.

Both strongly support that Bosentan reverses age-related regenerative decline (C6, C79-C82, C109). OpenEval finds aged mice achieving adult-level regeneration 'particularly compelling'; peer reviewers strongly affirm with Reviewer 1 emphasizing this counteracts aging effects and Reviewer 3 confirming findings are 'well supported.'

Both address ET-1 and ETBR levels during aging/injury (C75-C76). OpenEval notes elevated ET-1 provides mechanistic context but ETBR shows inconsistent changes; Reviewer 2 specifically questions these findings, asking about protein level changes and noting lack of injury-induced ETBR changes raises mechanistic questions.

Both support age-related SGC changes from snRNA-seq and TEM (C7, C88, C91-C93). OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from orthogonal methods showing quantitative and qualitative changes; peer reviewers accept findings as robust with Reviewer 3 noting 'decline in SGC numbers, morphological changes, and transcriptional reprogramming.'

Both address transcriptional reprogramming in aged SGCs (C85-C87). OpenEval includes pathway enrichment as part of comprehensive SGC aging evidence; Reviewer 3 acknowledges these findings as part of transcriptional changes that 'may impair pro-regenerative capacity.'

Major disagreement on mechanistic link between ETBR and Cx43 (C8, C101-C103, C106-C107). OpenEval supports correlation as consistent with literature, appropriately qualifying mechanism as speculative; peer reviewers express significant concerns with Reviewer 2 stating 'no direct evidence' and 'no functional evidence' that Cx43 acts downstream of ETBR. Reviewer 3 requests cell-type-specific knockouts to clarify the link.

Both support overarching therapeutic conclusion (C108, C110, C122-C123). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable hypotheses requiring validation and appropriately cautious therapeutic claims; peer reviewers strongly support with all three reviewers affirming this as an 'important study' with 'convincing evidence' and 'well supported' main conclusions, emphasizing therapeutic potential.

Both address speculative mechanisms (C111-C114, C116, C119, C121, C140, C144). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable hypotheses appropriately qualified as speculative requiring future validation; peer reviewers similarly acknowledge these as speculative, with Reviewer 3 noting the study 'does not provide complete mechanistic understanding' but speculation is 'appropriately addressed in the Discussion.'
